acceptedAnswer.text: Quick commerce marketing is the work of winning visibility and sales on apps that deliver in minutes, such as Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart, through better listings, well-placed sponsored ads and careful planning around what is in stock.

mainEntity.name: How does quick commerce advertising work with MMC?

acceptedAnswer.text: We make the listing legible at tile size, plan sponsored placements around availability, and review results every week at blended level, because app-level data is limited.

mainEntity.name: What does quick commerce advertising cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your ad spend is paid to the quick-commerce apps and sits outside our fee. We quote our fee after a call, once we have seen the account and agreed what we will run. We do not publish a price list, because the right scope depends on your spend and your margins.

No. We cannot guarantee visibility or sales on apps we do not control. We commit to well-made listings, careful placement and honest reporting, with results judged on contribution margin, not on what a platform reports.

mainEntity.name: Who is quick commerce advertising for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quick commerce is mainly a D2C channel, so this page leads with D2C brands that can supply dark stores. It also applies to B2B and education brands: the same method, measured on qualified leads, enquiries and admissions instead of orders.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us?

acceptedAnswer.text: App seller or brand panel access, your catalogue and margins, stock and replenishment visibility, and your pack and listing images.

leaks.note: Screens are illustrative recreations of each platform's interface, not client data. Platform names and logos belong to their owners.
leaks.lede: On quick-commerce apps, the tile, the placement and the stock decide the sale. Each stage below is where brands lose, and how we run it.

stages.breaks: Reusing marketplace images on a tile-sized screen.
stages.why: Shoppers scroll fast on a small screen. The image, name and claim must work in a second.
stages.does: We re-cut images, names and claims for tile-first browsing, so the product reads at a glance.

stages.why: Search and category placements behave differently, and spend is wasted where the product is not the obvious choice.
stages.does: We plan sponsored placements by the search terms and categories that fit the product, and adjust bids as results come in.

stages.breaks: Advertising where the product is not stocked.
stages.why: Each dark store serves a small area. If your product is out of stock there, an ad reaches shoppers who cannot buy it.
stages.does: We plan ads around availability by area, so spend follows where the product can actually be delivered.

stages.breaks: Treating stock as someone else's job.
stages.why: Out-of-stock products lose visibility and shoppers, and it can take time to win them back.
stages.does: We work with your supply team on availability signals and replenishment, so visibility does not lapse.

stages.breaks: Expecting clean attribution from each app.
stages.why: Platform data is limited, so app-level numbers can mislead.
stages.does: We read quick-commerce results alongside your total sales and margin, and judge the channel on what it adds to the business.
